in_vivo_species.quote: Studies were performed on 8- to 12-week old gender-matched C57BL/6 mice purchased from Charles River Laboratories (Wilmington, MA).

agents.name: V-Gem (5'-l-valyl-gemcitabine)
agents.sequence: not reported as a one-letter sequence; the body states the prodrug is formed by linking l-valine to gemcitabine via an ester bond
agents.sequence_source: INTRO: 'One such PEPT1-targeted gemcitabine prodrug, 5'-l-valyl-gemcitabine (V-Gem), was generated by linking l-valine to gemcitabine via an ester bond.' Figure 1 shows the chemical structure. The PEPLIFE2 header lists sequence 'V', which is metadata and not an evidence source.
agents.chemical_identifier: 5'-l-valyl-gemcitabine; synthesized by AAPharmaSyn, LLC (Ann Arbor, MI); LC-MS/MS parent ion m/z 363.1, product ion 264.0 (Table 1)
agents.group_n_quote: Pharmacokinetic parameters of Gem, dFdU, and V-Gem following IV (76 nmol/g) and PO (228 nmol/g) administrations of Gem and V-Gem in mice (n = 4).
agents.dose: 76 nmol/g body weight IV; 228 nmol/g body weight PO; 100 uM and 10 mM in perfusion solution for the in situ jejunal perfusions
agents.dose_route_quote: For oral studies, mice were fasted overnight (~ 16 hr) and subsequently administered 228 nmol/g body weight of Gem or V-Gem (in 0.2 mL water per 25 g body weight) via oral gavage (n=4).
agents.half_life: 3.7 min (33%) after intravenous V-Gem; could not be determined after oral dosing
agents.half_life_elimination: 3.7 min (33% geometric CV) after IV dosing; CND (could not be determined) after oral dosing
agents.cmax: 32.7 uM (139%) after IV (reported as C0 = Cmax); 0.2 uM (101%) after oral dosing
agents.tmax: not reported after IV (C0 reported instead); 3.5 min (range 2-5) after oral dosing
agents.auc: AUCinf 106 min x uM (98%) after IV; AUC0-6hr 1.9 min x uM (113%) after oral (AUCinf CND). Oral bioavailability 0.6%
agents.pk_quote: Following intravenous V-Gem administration, V-Gem reached an initial concentration (C0 = Cmax) of 32.7 uM and was rapidly eliminated with a T1/2 of 3.7 min.
agents.notes_agent: Additional reported V-Gem parameters after IV dosing: CL 43.1 mL/hr/g (98%), Vss 2.4 mL/g (145%). Parameters are geometric mean (geometric CV%) except Tmax, median (min-max).

agents.name: Gemcitabine (Gem, 2',2'-difluoro-2'-deoxycytidine, dFdC)
agents.sequence: not applicable (nucleoside analogue, not a peptide)
agents.chemical_identifier: 2',2'-difluoro-2'-deoxycytidine; purchased from Thermo Fisher Scientific; LC-MS/MS parent ion m/z 264.0, product ion 112.0 (Table 1)
agents.group_n_quote: Pharmacokinetic parameters of Gem, dFdU, and V-Gem following IV (76 nmol/g) and PO (228 nmol/g) administrations of Gem and V-Gem in mice (n = 4).
agents.dose: 76 nmol/g body weight IV (stated in Discussion as 20 mg gemcitabine/kg body weight); 228 nmol/g body weight PO; 100 uM and 10 mM in perfusion solution
agents.dose_route_quote: For intravenous studies, mice were administered 76 nmol/g body weight of Gem or V-Gem (in 0.1 mL saline per 25 g body weight) via bolus tail vein injection (n=4).
agents.half_life: 42.5 min (44%) after intravenous gemcitabine; 29.8 min (41%) after oral gemcitabine
agents.cmax: 67.2 uM (30%) after IV (reported as C0 = Cmax); 9.8 uM (42%) after oral dosing
agents.tmax: not reported after IV (C0 reported instead); 30 min (range 15-45) after oral dosing
agents.auc: AUCinf 1628 min x uM (38%) IV; 893 min x uM (55%) PO. Oral bioavailability 18.3%
agents.pk_quote: Following oral administration, Gem was rapidly absorbed reaching a maximum concentration (Cmax) of 9.8 uM at a Tmax of 30 min. The terminal half-life (T1/2) of Gem following intravenous Gem administration (42.5 min)
agents.notes_agent: After IV dosing CL was 2.8 mL/hr/g (38%) and Vss 1.4 mL/g (44%). Gemcitabine formed after V-Gem dosing had T1/2 46.2 min (IV, Tmax 2 min, Cmax 41.6 uM, AUCinf 801) and 39.1 min (PO, Tmax 15 min, Cmax 11.1 uM, AUCinf 814, bioavailability 16.7%).

agents.name: dFdU (2',2'-difluoro-2'-deoxyuridine)
agents.chemical_identifier: 2',2'-difluorodeoxyuridine, purchased from Sigma-Aldrich; LC-MS/MS parent ion m/z 265.0, product ion 113.0 (Table 1)
agents.group_n_quote: Pharmacokinetic parameters of Gem, dFdU, and V-Gem following IV (76 nmol/g) and PO (228 nmol/g) administrations of Gem and V-Gem in mice (n = 4).
agents.dose: not dosed; measured as the deaminated metabolite after Gem or V-Gem administration. Also purchased as an authentic standard for calibrators and quality controls
agents.dose_route_quote: Tetrahydrouridine (THU) and the deaminated gemcitabine metabolite 2',2'-difluorodeoxyuridine (dFdU) were purchased from Sigma-Aldrich
agents.half_life: 106 min (32%) after IV Gem; 210 min (41%) after oral Gem; 128 min (38%) after IV V-Gem; 216 min (9%) after oral V-Gem
agents.half_life_elimination: 106 min (IV Gem); 210 min (PO Gem); 128 min (IV V-Gem); 216 min (PO V-Gem)
agents.cmax: 15.5 uM (IV Gem); 35.3 uM (PO Gem); 13.9 uM (IV V-Gem); 47.9 uM (PO V-Gem)
agents.tmax: 30 min, range 30-45 (IV Gem); 45 min, range 30-120 (PO Gem); 22.5 min, range 15-30 (IV V-Gem); 30 min, range 15-30 (PO V-Gem)
agents.auc: AUCinf 2484 min x uM (IV Gem); 8613 (PO Gem); 2345 (IV V-Gem); 11,125 (PO V-Gem)
agents.pk_quote: The T1/2 of dFdU was shorter following intravenous Gem administration (106 min), as compared to the T1/2 after oral Gem administration (210 min) (p = 0.050).
agents.notes_agent: These are metabolite half-lives measured after parent-drug dosing, not half-lives of an administered dose of dFdU. The Discussion cautions that the sampling scheme 'may bias downward estimates of dFdU T1/2'.

concentration_time_figure.locator: Figs. 2-6 (Fig. 4 for V-Gem IV, Fig. 5 for V-Gem oral)
concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Mean plasma concentration-time profiles of Gem, dFdU, and V-Gem following intravenous (IV) administration of 76 nmol V-Gem/g body weight in mice.
concentration_time_figure.note: Mean plasma concentration versus time on linear and logarithmic axes, mean ± SE, n = 4, for Gem and dFdU after IV Gem (Fig. 2) and oral Gem (Fig. 3), and for Gem, dFdU and V-Gem after IV V-Gem (Fig. 4) and oral V-Gem (Fig. 5). Fig. 6 overlays the oral Gem and oral V-Gem profiles. Fig. 7 is a portal plasma bar chart, not a concentration-time plot.

bioanalytical_method: LC-MS/MS for plasma pharmacokinetic samples (Shimadzu HPLC with Applied Biosystems API 4000 QTRAP, positive-mode MRM, Agilent Poroshell 120 EC-C18 column, 13C,15N2-Gem and 13C,15N2-dFdU internal standards); UPLC with photodiode array detection (Waters Acquity H-Class, Acquity HSS T3 column, caffeine internal standard) for portal plasma and intestinal perfusate samples
bioanalytical_quote: The concentrations of Gem, dFdU, and V-Gem were determined in mouse plasma samples using a novel LC-MS/MS method utilizing a Shimadzu HPLC system ... coupled with an Applied Biosystems API 4000 triple quadrupole/linear ion trap (QTRAP) mass spectrometer
notes: Cmax and Tmax are reported for every analyte and are captured above; note that for intravenous dosing the table footnote states 'C0 reported for Cmax', so the IV Cmax values (Gem 67.2 uM, V-Gem 32.7 uM) are back-extrapolated initial concentrations rather than observed peaks, and no IV Tmax is given. Oral Tmax values (Gem 30 min, V-Gem 3.5 min, dFdU 45 min) reflect absorption but the paper reports NO absorption half-life and NO absorption rate constant anywhere, so half_life_absorption is 'not reported' throughout and nothing was converted. All T1/2 values are the terminal half-life from non-compartmental analysis in Phoenix WinNonlin 8.2: 'The terminal half-life (T1/2) of Gem following intravenous Gem administration (42.5 min)'. Parameters are geometric mean (geometric CV%) except Tmax (median, min-max) and Foral (dose-normalised AUCinf ratio). CND in Table 3 means could not be determined. Per-analyte values that could not fit the single headline fields are preserved in pk_quote and notes_agent. Procedural and bioanalytical agents not treated as study articles: sodium pentobarbital (40-60 mg/kg intraperitoneal) for perfusion anaesthesia, tetrahydrouridine (THU) added to collection tubes to block ex vivo deamination, EDTA-K3 anticoagulant, and the stable-isotope internal standards 13C,15N2-Gem and 13C,15N2-dFdU. Study_types lists only in vivo: the single-pass jejunal perfusion is performed in situ in an anaesthetised living mouse, and the blank-mouse-plasma calibrator/stability samples are bioanalytical assay validation rather than an ex vivo treatment study. Prior in vitro work with recombinant human CDA, Caco-2 monolayers and simulated gastric fluid is cited in the Discussion as previous studies, not performed here.
